item.text:
## 1B.9 Research Note: Bongbong Marcos in 2024

**Working judgment:** **Partial yes.** Marcos’s 2024 record shows real movement on **cybersecurity precaution, public reporting, and digital-government transparency**, but the evidence is much weaker on **biological risk** and **AI safety governance**, and some of the same year’s defense moves pushed further into **dual-use cyber/information-warfare capacity**.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| Favorable | [PBBM approves National Cybersecurity Plan to fortify PH against various threats](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-approves-national-cybersecurity-plan-to-fortify-ph-against-various-threats/) | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-02-08 | https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-approves-national-cybersecurity-plan-to-fortify-ph-against-various-threats/ | Marcos approved the National Cybersecurity Plan 2024-2029, presented as a policy-direction document with operational guidelines. The release says it was developed with public, private, and academic stakeholders, which is the clearest precaution/transparency signal I found. | `1B.9`, `1B.7` |
| Favorable | [PBBM adopts DICT’s National Cybersecurity Plan 2023-2028](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-adopts-dicts-national-cybersecurity-plan-2023-2028/) | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-04-06 | https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-adopts-dicts-national-cybersecurity-plan-2023-2028/ | EO 58 made the NCSP a whole-of-nation roadmap and required agencies and LGUs to implement and report on it. This is stronger evidence of institutionalized cyber precaution than of ad hoc personal control. | `1B.9`, `1B.7` |
| Favorable / mixed | [Marcos supports AFP bid to beef up cybersecurity capabilities](https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1228276) | Philippine News Agency | 2024-07-04 | https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1228276 | Marcos backed military cyber-capability upgrades and new tactics against cybersecurity threats. That is precautionary capacity-building, but it is aimed at capability rather than transparency or civilian oversight. | `1B.9`, `1B.3`, `1B.7` |
| Favorable / mixed | [Gov’t vows legal action vs deep fake video creators, spreaders](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/govt-vows-legal-action-vs-deep-fake-video-creators-spreaders/) | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-04-26 | https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/govt-vows-legal-action-vs-deep-fake-video-creators-spreaders/ | After a deepfake video of Marcos, the government said DICT and the NSC were investigating and that legal action was being considered. This shows reactive handling of an information-risk incident, though it is not a broad AI safety regime. | `1B.9`, `1B.7`, `1B.8` |
| Favorable / low-specificity | [MSMEs should be AI-ready - PBBM](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/msmes-should-be-ai-ready-pbbm/) | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-04-30 | https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/msmes-should-be-ai-ready-pbbm/ | Marcos publicly pushed AI adoption for MSMEs, framing it as practical use rather than technical theory. This is pro-adoption and institution-building, but it is not evidence of AI safety, audit, or risk governance. | `1B.9`, `1B.7` |
| Mixed / limiting | [Marcos signs self-reliant defense posture law](https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1234986) | Philippine News Agency | 2024-10-08 | https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1234986 | Marcos signed a law expanding local defense-tech capacity and explicitly naming cyber security breaches, chemical attacks, radiological threats, AI, robotics, and cyber defense. This is serious dual-use expansion, but I found no matching transparency or safeguard architecture in the same record. | `1B.9`, `1B.3`, `1B.7` |
| Critical | [Philippines, US to hold military drills in islands facing South China Sea, Taiwan](https://www.yahoo.com/news/philippines-us-hold-military-drills-074919409.html) | Reuters | 2024-03-05 | https://www.yahoo.com/news/philippines-us-hold-military-drills-074919409.html | Balikatan 2024 included cyber/information-warfare training near sensitive islands. That is direct evidence of dual-use cyber capacity being exercised in a deterrence-heavy setting, which cuts against a strong precaution/transparency reading. | `1B.9`, `1B.3`, `1B.1` |
| Favorable / transparency context | [PH takes strides toward transparency](https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1217036) | Philippine News Agency | 2024-01-18 | https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1217036 | The government expanded public access through the eFOI portal and kept a media-literacy / disinformation campaign in place. This supports a general transparency posture in digital governance, but it is not direct evidence of catastrophic-risk management. | `1B.9` |

### Synthesis

- **Best evidence for precaution/transparency:** the National Cybersecurity Plan was adopted with consultation and implementation/reporting requirements.
- **Best evidence against a strong reading:** Marcos also expanded **dual-use defense-tech** and **cyber/information-warfare** capacity, with little public evidence of corresponding oversight or safety rules.
- **Search gap:** I found **no reliable 2024 evidence** of a substantive Marcos-led **biosecurity / biological-risk** agenda, and no clear **AI safety or model-governance** framework. The evidence is strongest on **cyber defense and digital governance**, weaker on catastrophic-risk domains more broadly.

**Working judgment for 1B.9:** **Partial yes.** Marcos handled cyber and some digital-risk issues with real precaution and some transparency, but the record does **not** show a comprehensive precautionary posture across all high-risk dual-use domains.
